story.vex: One key, one copy, and now two owners. Guess which one isn't you. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED. The old key opens nothing anymore. Astro: "One shared key is one point of failure. Rotate it before it costs us."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
The crew radio uses one shared key for everyone, and Doom found a copy. Prove the leaked key still opens our traffic, then rotate to a new one Doom does not have.

1. type intercepted-traffic.txt
2. xor codexia7 <the intercepted hex>
3. submit the decoded message
4. type new-key-orders.txt
5. xor relay-9x <the new plaintext, all caps>
6. submit the new ciphertext (Rivet checks it against the radio log)
files.C:\\Citadel\\intercepted-traffic.txt:
Old shared key: codexia7
Intercepted (hex): 30272d20342d3217223b44232d252d
Decode with: xor codexia7 <hex>
files.C:\\Citadel\\new-key-orders.txt:
Rivet: rotate to the new key relay-9x. Encode this exact message with it, all capitals, one space between words: NEW KEY ACTIVE
Encode with: xor relay-9x NEW KEY ACTIVE

steps.title: Prove the leaked key still works
steps.body: Volt: "If the leaked key still opens our traffic, we have to assume Doom is reading everything." Read `intercepted-traffic.txt`, then run `xor codexia7 1a0a0716454d0e470b52021a06` and submit exactly what it decodes to.

steps.title: Rotate the key
steps.body: Rivet: "New key, Cadet. Doom doesn't get a copy this time." Read `new-key-orders.txt`, then run `xor relay-9x NEW KEY ACTIVE` and submit the ciphertext it produces.
